components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type

          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status

          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp

          type: string

## Change: owners may carry a validated, lower-cased `email`

**Spec behaviour** — an owner may include `email`; when present it must be a syntactically valid address, is stored and returned lower-cased, and an invalid value is rejected with 400 (absent is accepted).

### Files changed

- **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `email` property (`format: email`, `maxLength: 255`) to the `OwnerFields` schema, so both the request DTO (`OwnerFieldsDto`) and response DTO (`OwnerDto`) gain the field via code generation.
- **`model/Owner.java`** — added the `email` column with getter/setter. MapStruct now maps it both ways by name automatically.
- **DB schemas** (`hsqldb`, `h2`, `mysql`, `postgres` `schema.sql`) — added the `email` column to the `owners` table.
- **DB seed data** (`hsqldb`, `mysql` `data.sql`) — the positional `INSERT INTO owners VALUES (...)` statements would break against the new column, so I gave them explicit column lists (`h2`/`postgres` already used explicit lists).
- **`function/owner/OwnerEmail.java`** (new) — shared helper mirroring `OwnerTelephone`: `isValid(...)` (syntactic check) and `normalize(...)` (trim + lower-case, null for blank).
- **`function/owner/ValidateNewOwner.java`** — on `POST`, when an email is supplied it is normalized and rejected via a new checked `InvalidEmailException` if invalid, then stored lower-cased.
- **`function/owner/ApplyOwner.java`** — on `PUT`, the email is applied lower-cased (the generated `@Email` on the `@Valid` body already rejects invalid values there).
- **`escalation/InvalidEmailException.java` + `InvalidEmailExceptionHandler.java` + the matching `officefloor/escalation/...InvalidEmailException.yml`** (new) — follow the existing telephone pattern, responding `400` with `{"errors":["email"]}`.

### Tests
`AcceptanceTest` (lowercases a mixed-case email, rejects `not-an-email` with 400, accepts a missing email) and the full suite are green: `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`.

I kept the handler consistent with the existing `InvalidTelephoneException` style rather than inventing a new error shape. No commit was made, since you didn't ask for one.
